title: Be a Doctor
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for Shellfie.

pages: Today, you are a children's doctor! A doctor for kids is called a pediatrician.
You work in a doctor's office, and sometimes in a hospital. You wear a white coat, and you carry a stethoscope to listen to hearts and lungs.
Your first patient is a baby who came for a checkup. You measure how long she is and how much she weighs. She has grown so much!
Next, a boy has a sore throat. You look inside with a little light. "Say ahh!" He says "ahh" so loudly that the nurse covers her ears.
A girl hides under the table because she does not want her shot. You hide under there too, and you both count to three. She says it only felt like a tiny pinch.
Then a little boy asks, "Can I listen to YOUR heart?" You let him. He says, "It sounds like a drum!"
You work with a team: nurses, medical assistants, the people at the front desk, and pharmacists who give out medicine.
The best part? You help kids feel better, and you see them grow up strong.
The hardest part? Some days are very long. Sometimes you get called in the middle of the night, and sometimes you must tell a family hard news.
How do you become a doctor? Go to college for 4 years, then medical school for 4 years, then train in a hospital for about 3 more years. That is about 11 years!
What can you do now? Learn first aid. Ask your own doctor questions at your checkup. Play doctor with a toy kit, and learn how your body works.

quiz.q: What does a doctor use to listen to hearts?
quiz.ev: you carry a stethoscope to listen to hearts and lungs

quiz.q: Why did the doctor hide under the table too?
o: To help the girl feel brave
quiz.ev: You hide under there too, and you both count to three.
A doctor for kids is called a pediatrician.
